question: A 74-year-old woman is brought to the clinic because her family reports progressive forgetfulness over the past two years. She now has difficulty managing her finances and gets lost in familiar places. Neurologic examination is otherwise normal. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis? A) Alzheimer disease B) Normal pressure hydrocephalus C) Major depressive disorder D) Vitamin B12 deficiency
Which of the following medications is a cholinesterase inhibitor used to treat mild to moderate Alzheimer disease? A) Donepezil B) Memantine C) Haloperidol D) Lorazepam

An 80-year-old man has well-formed visual hallucinations, fluctuating alertness and mild parkinsonism. He developed severe rigidity after a single dose of haloperidol. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis? A) Dementia with Lewy bodies B) Vascular dementia C) Frontotemporal dementia D) Creutzfeldt-Jakob disease

Which of the following is a typical early feature of behavioral variant frontotemporal dementia? A) Disinhibition and apathy B) Early visual hallucinations C) Stepwise decline after strokes D) Rapidly progressive myoclonus

Which finding on brain imaging is most characteristic of early Alzheimer disease? A) Atrophy of the medial temporal lobe and hippocampus B) Hot cross bun sign in the pons C) Hummingbird sign of the midbrain D) Cortical ribboning on diffusion-weighted MRI
